title: Wittich: antecedent, essential, and accidental acts — remission-fiducia not of the essence
source_text: XXXII. Christophorus Wittichius, jam ante memoratus, distinguit actus fidem antecedentes, actus fidei essentiales, & actus fidei accidentales, & qui solum fidei corroboratae conveniunt. Juxta ipsum, actus fidem antecedens est notitia revelationis. Actus vero fidei essentialis primus, est assensus, tum generalis omnibus revelatis, tum specialis huic veritati, quod Christus sit sufficiens salvator omnibus ad se confugientibus, adeoque etiam mihi, si serio desiderem justitiam, atque ad Christum confugere velim. Secundus actus fidei essentialis est amor Christi sincerus qui statim oritur ex quo Christus cognitus est, tanquam objectum conveniens, & sit apprehensus per assensum istum fiducialem. Tertius est fiducia, qua nobis persuademus auxilium certum nos accepturos a Christo salvatore in omnibus angustiis & tentationibus, innixi promissionibus factis omnibus ad se confugientibus. Actus vero accidentales, & qui solum fidei corroboratae conveniunt, sunt, primo, fiducia de remissione peccatorum a Deo impetrata; secundo, solidum gaudium ex illorum notitia; tertio, pax & tranquillitas conscientiae. Quod latius explicans, observat ad fidei justificantis essentiam, sive rationem formalem, non requiri fiduciam remissionis peccatorum, sive in praeterito, sive in futuro, sed eam esse effectum fidei magis corroboratae & plenae. Quoniam experientia docet infirmos quosdam fideles revera habere fidem, qui habent famem & sitim justitiae, qui tamen nondum possunt sibi propter suam imbecillitatem persuadere, quod habeant, vel sint consecuturi remissionem peccatorum. In Theologia Pacifica, cap. 11. n. 138.
pass_a_gloss: Christopher Wittich, already mentioned before, distinguishes acts antecedent to faith, essential acts of faith, and accidental acts of faith, and those which belong only to corroborated faith. According to him, the act antecedent to faith is knowledge of revelation. But the first essential act of faith is assent, both general to all things revealed, and special to this truth, that Christ is a sufficient Savior for all who flee to Him, and so also for me, if I seriously desire justice and wish to flee to Christ. The second essential act of faith is sincere love of Christ which arises at once from the moment Christ is known as a fitting object, and has been apprehended by that fiducial assent. The third is trust by which we persuade ourselves that we shall receive sure help from Christ the Savior in all straits and temptations, leaning on the promises made to all who flee to Him. But the accidental acts, and those which belong only to corroborated faith, are: first, trust concerning remission of sins obtained from God; second, solid joy from the knowledge of them; third, peace and tranquillity of conscience. Explaining this more widely, he observes that for the essence, or formal reason, of justifying faith, trust of remission of sins — whether past or future — is not required, but that it is an effect of faith more corroborated and full. Since experience teaches that certain weak faithful truly have faith, who have hunger and thirst for justice, who yet because of their weakness cannot yet persuade themselves that they have, or shall obtain, remission of sins. In Theologia Pacifica, chapter 11, number 138.
pass_b_english: Essential: general+special assent (Christ sufficient for me if I flee); sincere love of Christ; fiducia of sure help in straits.
Accidental/corroborated: fiducia of obtained remission; solid joy; peace of conscience.
Remission-fiducia is not of justifying faith’s essence — effect of fuller faith.
Weak believers may hunger for justice without yet persuading themselves of remission.
